subject: Region tagging and deletion authority - clarification and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <security@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Region tagging and deletion authority - initial questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking the time to speak last week. We’re getting our internal legal and infosec teams aligned and they sent over a compact set of clarifying questions about how Redwood would support per-tenant regional storage, regional retention TTLs, and the ability for our data owners to trigger deletions in-region.

Top items they want clarified:
- Can tenants be pinned to a specific physical region and prevent cross-region fallback?
- Is there an admin-level API for initiating an on-demand erase that operates only within the tenant’s region?
- What audit evidence can Redwood provide when a deletion is executed (log entries, KMS key IDs, retention policy id)?
- If we request an export prior to deletion, how long is the export retained and where is it stored?

I’ve attached their questionnaire (acme_data_retention_questions.pdf). We’re aiming for a contract signature by end of Q3, but these controls are gating for our procurement / privacy review. Can you loop in product and engineering and let us know what’s feasible and an approximate delivery timeline if something needs to be built?

Thanks — Jordan
Security Program Manager
AcmeHealth

Attachment: acme_data_retention_questions.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region tagging and deletion authority - initial questions

Hi Jordan — thanks for sending this.

Quick answers up front: we can pin a tenant to a preferred region today; we also support explicit region routing for reads/writes, but the strict "no-fallback" mode you described needs a small enhancement to the routing policy layer. On-demand erase APIs exist in our private deployments, and we can surface an admin endpoint for hosted customers behind an enterprise feature flag.

I’ve asked Markus and Grace to outline the implementation details and an estimated timeline. For audit evidence, our standard deliverable includes timestamped audit log entries, the storage object IDs that were deleted, and the KMS key identifiers used to crypto-shred objects where applicable. We can also provide a signed attestation artifact for an extra compliance cost.

Proposed next steps:
1) Markus to confirm what parts are product vs platform work and estimate ETA.
2) We’ll draft a scoped SOW addendum (I attached a rough proposal: redwood_proposal_draft_v1.pdf).
3) If Acme wants, we can run a tabletop with Procurement + Infosec to walk through deletion flows before signing.

Would it help if we scoped a conservative timeline (MVP within 8 weeks, GA in 14) assuming dedicated engineering allocation?

—So
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_proposal_draft_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Miles <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region tagging and deletion authority - technical approach and constraints

Hi team — following up with technical context and a proposal for how we’d implement the ask with minimal product churn. High level:

Summary of current behavior:
- Tenant assignment: tenants have a "preferred_region" metadata field today used by the smart router for low-latency placement.
- Fallbacks: for HA we currently allow cross-region fallback to keep the service available if a region is degraded. This fallback path copies runtime state into a compatible region.
- Deletion API: internal admin delete endpoints exist but are not surfaced as self-serve for hosted customers. Deletions are recorded in audit logs with object ids and timestamps.

Proposed minimal-scope changes for AcmeHealth:
1) Strict region pinning toggle (policy): an opt-in tenant flag that disables cross-region fallback for reads/writes and KV replication. This prevents any automatic copies outside the pinned region.
2) On-demand erase endpoint: expose an admin API (POST /admin/tenants/{id}/erase) that triggers a region-local deletion flow and emits structured audit records. The flow will:
   - Create a pre-deletion export snapshot (optional) written to the tenant's region into an export bucket tagged with export-job-id and retention TTL.
   - Execute object-level deletion + metadata purge.
   - Emit an audit artifact: deletion_job_id, list of deleted object IDs, timestamps, KMS key ids used.
3) Audit attestation: signed artifact generation option (HSM-backed signing) as an add-on.

Engineering notes / risks:
- Disabling fallback reduces our HA options; we must document SLO deviations and get product sign-off.
- Export snapshot retention: by default we keep exports for 7 days; can be parameterized on a per-job basis but that’s extra storage and governance cost.
- Cross-region replicas already present (historical) will need a one-time scrub when strict pinning is enabled; we’ll add a migration job to locate and remove stale replicas. This is the largest work item if Acme already has historical data outside the target region.

ETA estimates (assuming dedicated sprint capacity):
- Policy toggle + config: 2 weeks (design + admin UI + API)
- Erase endpoint + local flow + audit records: 4 weeks
- Export snapshot opt-in + retention parameter: 1 week
- Migration/replica scrub tooling (if needed): 2-3 weeks (depends on scale)

If Acme requires signed attestation + HSM path, add 3 weeks for secure signing integration and compliance checks.

I recommend we propose an MVP that includes the region pinning toggle and the on-demand erase endpoint with default 7-day export retention. We can then offer migration tooling as a pre-signature engagement if they confirm cross-region historical replicas exist.

—Markus
Director, Platform Engineering
